Code Review by Qodo

🐞 Bugs (1) 📘 Rule violations (0) 📜 Skill insights (0)
1. Scratch copies can fill the runner disk ✓ Resolved
>
>Description >
> >
>run_task retains each attempt's workspace tar, extracted snapshot and diff copies under work_dir
>after the rep is finished. With multiple reps or reruns containing large workspaces, these copies
>accumulate even though the workspace size limit applies separately to each snapshot.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[hb/orchestrator.py[R429-431]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/pull/3/files#diff-8e7c4737f7a46e821465b9e891d0783336d86dfd71d6927cac7ff112379991c7R429-R431) > >```diff >+ for rep in range(1, suite["reps"] + 1): >+ result, attempts = run_rep(job, cohort, rep, docker=docker, clock=clock, pristine=pristine, >+ work=work_dir, timing=timing) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>An attempt writes a workspace tar and extracts a snapshot into its scratch directory; the rep loop
>creates a different scratch path for each attempt and never removes those paths. The suite schema
>permits up to ten reps, and the snapshot limit permits up to 1 GiB of files per attempt.
>
> > [hb/orchestrator.py\[266-272\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/66b5bbbd7a47d0c3b157ae620f90b21654c339ea/hb/orchestrator.py/#L266-L272) > [hb/orchestrator.py\[299-310\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/66b5bbbd7a47d0c3b157ae620f90b21654c339ea/hb/orchestrator.py/#L299-L310) > [hb/orchestrator.py\[333-339\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/66b5bbbd7a47d0c3b157ae620f90b21654c339ea/hb/orchestrator.py/#L333-L339) > [hb/orchestrator.py\[428-451\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/66b5bbbd7a47d0c3b157ae620f90b21654c339ea/hb/orchestrator.py/#L428-L451) > [schemas/common.schema.json\[80-84\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/66b5bbbd7a47d0c3b157ae620f90b21654c339ea/schemas/common.schema.json/#L80-L84) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Attempt scratch directories retain large workspace copies throughout the task, allowing later reps to exhaust runner storage. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- hb/orchestrator.py[266-272] >- hb/orchestrator.py[333-347] >- hb/orchestrator.py[428-451] > >## Recommended Fix >Remove each attempt's scratch directory after its patch and logs have been captured, including void attempts. Keep only data required for grading and bundle assembly, and clean up the task scratch directory on completion or failure. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
2. Harnesses can run past their kill deadline ✓ Resolved
>
>Description >
> >
>_watch_harness gives a gateway-log copy at least one second even when less than one second remains
>before the wall or budget-grace deadline. If that copy blocks near either deadline, the loop cannot
>kill the harness until the read returns or times out.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[hb/orchestrator.py[247]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/pull/3/files#diff-8e7c4737f7a46e821465b9e891d0783336d86dfd71d6927cac7ff112379991c7R247-R247) > >```diff >+ _poll_records(docker, gateway, tail, timeout=max(1.0, min(LOG_READ_TIMEOUT_S, next_deadline - now))) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The loop kills only after checking deadlines on its next iteration, while the log-copy timer can
>hold that iteration for the one-second minimum.
>
> > [hb/orchestrator.py\[234-257\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/66b5bbbd7a47d0c3b157ae620f90b21654c339ea/hb/orchestrator.py/#L234-L257) > [hb/dockercli.py\[138-163\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/66b5bbbd7a47d0c3b157ae620f90b21654c339ea/hb/dockercli.py/#L138-L163) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >A gateway-log read can outlast the remaining wall-clock or budget-grace time because its timeout is clamped to at least one second. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- hb/orchestrator.py[234-257] > >## Recommended Fix >Use the actual positive time remaining as the log-copy timeout, and recheck the deadline before starting a read when no time remains. Add a test with a slow log read immediately before a fractional-second deadline. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
3. Gateway log is re-copied in full every poll 🐞 Bug ➹ Performance
>
>Description >
> >
>_watch_harness calls _poll_records about every poll_s (2 s). Each call runs docker cp on the
>whole /log/gateway.jsonl and buffers it in memory through read_single_file, and only then does
>RecordTail.feed throw away everything before self.offset. Over a long rep the total copy and
>parse work grows with the square of the log size, up to 256 MiB per poll. The per-poll
>LOG_READ_TIMEOUT_S and the caller swallowing DockerError/TransferError mean a slow copy just
>ends without a result, so the early upstream_failed and budget-refusal detection quietly stops
>working once the log is large.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[hb/orchestrator.py[R183-187]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/pull/3/files#diff-8e7c4737f7a46e821465b9e891d0783336d86dfd71d6927cac7ff112379991c7R183-R187) > >```diff >+def _poll_records(docker: Docker, gateway: str, tail: RecordTail, timeout: float) -> None: >+ try: >+ tail.feed(_read_gateway_log(docker, gateway, timeout)) >+ except (DockerError, TransferError): >+ pass # a copy can fail while the log grows; the final read after the gateway stops decides >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>_read_gateway_log copies the entire file each time (copy_out + read_single_file, capped only at
>MAX_GATEWAY_LOG_BYTES). RecordTail.feed takes the full buffer and slices from self.offset, so the
>earlier bytes are transferred and decoded again on every poll. _watch_harness calls this inside
>its loop with sleeps of at most poll_s. Errors, timeouts included, are silently ignored in
>_poll_records.
>
> > [hb/orchestrator.py\[141-159\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/66b5bbbd7a47d0c3b157ae620f90b21654c339ea/hb/orchestrator.py/#L141-L159) > [hb/orchestrator.py\[178-187\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/66b5bbbd7a47d0c3b157ae620f90b21654c339ea/hb/orchestrator.py/#L178-L187) > [hb/orchestrator.py\[234-257\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/66b5bbbd7a47d0c3b157ae620f90b21654c339ea/hb/orchestrator.py/#L234-L257) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >While the harness runs, the orchestrator copies the whole gateway log out of the container on every poll (every 2 s), even though it only parses lines after `RecordTail.offset`. The cost grows with the log size, and slow copies time out silently, which turns off early void and budget detection. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- hb/orchestrator.py[178-187] >- hb/orchestrator.py[234-257] > >## Recommended Fix >Read only the tail you have not seen yet. One option: `docker exec`-free reads aren't possible because the gateway is read-only, so instead have the gateway also write a small marker file (for example `/log/state.json` with the first refusal time and a void flag) and poll only that. The other option is to back off polling as the log grows, e.g. poll the full log only when `docker container inspect`/a size check shows it grew, and widen the interval with size. Also log, rather than silently swallow, repeated poll failures. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
